Corners and the same-end structure. Multiply the decomposition of step 1.1 by the idempotents $e(n,i)$ on the left and $e(n,j)$ on the right. For $a\le n$ the term $e(n,i)\tau_n\cdots\tau_a$ lies in the corner with first letter $i$ and last letter $i$; moving the idempotent past the crossings with [F2] shows that for $i\ne j$ the summands with $a>1$ vanish on the right idempotent $e(n,j)$ (the last strand carries the color $i$), while for $i=j$ the top summand $e(n,i)R(n,1)e(n,i)$ survives for every $a$. The explicit degree of $\tau_n\cdots\tau_a$ on a fixed word is the sum of the crossing degrees $-b$ along the word, and the PBW leading terms show that $e(n,i)R(n+1)e(n,j)\cong q^{-(\alpha_i|\alpha_j)}\bigl(R(n)e(n-1,j)\otimes_{R(n-1)}e(n-1,i)R(n)\bigr)$ for $i\ne j$ and $e(n,i)R(n+1)e(n,i)\cong q^{-2d_i}\bigl(R(n)e(n-1,i)\otimes_{R(n-1)}e(n-1,i)R(n)\bigr)\oplus e(n,i)R(n,1)e(n,i)$ for $i=j$; the displayed shifts are exactly the source's $q^{-(\alpha_i|\alpha_j)}$ and $q^{-(\alpha_i|\alpha_i)}$.

The opposite-end exact sequence. By the same PBW-coset argument applied to the pair $(R(n),R_1(n))$ with $R_1(n)$ the image of the shift embedding $\xi_n$, the multiplication map $R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)$ is injective with image $\sum_{a=2}^{n+1}R(n,1)\tau_n\cdots\tau_a$, and the complementary coset $R(n,1)\tau_n\cdots\tau_1$ is free of rank one generated by $\tau_n\cdots\tau_1$ over $R(n,1)\cong R(n)\otimes k[x_{n+1}]$. The quotient map $\phi$ sends a PBW monomial to its coefficient on that coset, and the left multiplication by $x_{n+1}$ and the right multiplication by $x_1$ correspond under $\phi$ to multiplication by $t$ on $R(n)\otimes_kk[t]$; hence the displayed exact sequence of $(R(n),R(n))$-bimodules.

Tensor the corner isomorphisms of step 2.1 with the formulation $E_iF_j(N)=e(\beta,i)R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,j)\otimes_{R(\beta)}N$ and $F_iE_i(M)=R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)\otimes_{R(\beta)}e(\beta,i)M$. Apply step 2.2 to $\beta+\alpha_i$ in place of $n$, restrict along $e(\beta,i)$ and tensor over $R(\beta)$ with $M$; since the first term of step 2.2 is exactly the kernel of the left-append induction and the quotient is $R(\beta)\otimes_kk[t_i]$, the resulting sequence is $0\to\bar F_iE_iM\to E_i\bar F_iM\to q^{-(\alpha_i|\beta)}M\otimes_kk[t_i]\to0$, functorially in $M$, with the single q-shift coming from the difference of degrees between the two ends of the surviving coset, namely $-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$. Exactness of all functors is [F3].

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$. The bimodules $eA$ and $Ae$ are ungraded free respectively as left and right $B$-modules, of rank $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent $B$-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ the right-module summand $e(\xi)B$ has shift $\delta_R(w,\xi)=\deg(\tau_we(\xi))$ and the left-module summand $Be(\xi)$ has shift $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)=\delta_R(w,w^{-1}\xi)$, using respectively the corresponding right and left minimal shuffle representatives $w$; these degrees depend on the labels, and no common shift for an entire $B$ copy is asserted. The functors $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ and $\mathrm{Res}=e(-)$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. $\mathrm{Ind}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}$. The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded $B$-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic $E_i/F_i$ biadjunction theorem.
